children: Chicago corn firmed on Tuesday, supported by excessive rains in the US Midwest that slowed the harvest, while soybeans edged lower after closing higher in the last session.
Wheat prices ticked lower, although disruption to global supplies amid the Russia-Ukraine war limited the downside.
* The most-active corn contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT)
rose 0.1% to $4.97-1/2 a bushel, as of 0006 GMT, and soybeans fell 0.1% to $12.80 a bushel.
* US farmers have harvested 23% of their corn and 25% of their soybeans, below the average pace over the past five years, the US Department of Agriculture said on Monday.

* While rain has significantly slowed progress in parts of the western Midwest, particularly in Iowa, weather forecasts call for dry weather for much of this week across the central US. That drier weather could help speed up the harvest, market analysts said.
* The wheat market has been supported in recent weeks by the Russia-Ukraine war disrupting supplies. On Monday, a major Saudi purchase supported prices.
* Wall Street equities were buoyed by advances in mega-cap stocks on Monday, as Treasury yields held near multi-year highs, the dollar advanced against the euro, and oil prices relented.
